title: What fraction of the rectangle is blue?
description: Two blue triangles stand on the top and bottom sides of a rectangle, with their tips meeting at a point inside. Each has a full side as its base, and their heights add up to the width, so the blue part is half of the rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: two triangles on opposite sides of a rectangle have heights that add up to the width, so their areas add up to half of the rectangle. Watch for students who think the answer depends on where the tips meet.

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 4)
video_script.why: The child applies the add two triangle areas on a shared line method of the solved example, here with two heights that add up to the width.
video_script.substitution: Find each blue triangle from its base and height, add the two areas, and add the two heights first.

maths_rules: let the rectangle have length L and width W; each blue triangle has a full side of length L as its base
the heights of the two triangles are h1 (from the meeting point to the top side) and h2 (to the bottom side), and h1 + h2 = W
rectangle = L × W, so blue is 1/2 of the rectangle wherever the tips meet
check: an 8 by 5 rectangle with h1 = 2 and h2 = 3: 1/2 × 8 × 2 + 1/2 × 8 × 3 = 8 + 12 = 20, which is 1/2 of 40
video_script.design: One rectangle all video. Each blue triangle is read for its base and height and the heights are added first. The check uses made-up numbers.
open_questions: The figure is not in the extracted book text, so the two blue triangles follow the worklist: one on the top side and one on the bottom side, with their tips meeting at a point inside.
